messages.author: 563435cd1cb6a261
messages.subject: URI Rewrites
parts:
Hi,

I was wondering whether it is possible to do URI Rewrites likes in
Apache e.g:

RewriteRule ^/([^/]+)/([^/]+)$ index.php?x=foo&y=bar [L]

Such that a request to http://example.org/foo/bar would pass server.R
the x and y params.

If possible, I would appreciate a small compact example that does
something like above.

Thanks!

-Sarven
http://csarven.ca/#i

messages.author: 563435cd1cb6a261
messages.subject: Re: URI Rewrites
parts:
Hi Joe,

In case your email client ate up my email, you can see the source here:

https://groups.google.com/group/shiny-discuss/msg/1544f47c0ab777d5?dmode=source&output=gplain&noredirect

I'll elaborate:

What I'm trying to do is to have a proper URI mechanism where unique
URIs would make unique requests to the Shiny server. Plain ol' URI
rewriting.

To build on my example:

Intention is for http://example.org/foo/bar to show a scatter plot,
where foo is the x variable and bar is the y variable.

Similarly, http://example.org/foo/baz would show a scatter plot, where
foo is the x variable and baz is the y variable.

Hence, something needs to do along the lines of what Apache does:
RewriteRule ^/([^/]+)/([^/]+)$ index.php?x=foo&y=bar [L]

Although this is not the job of URI rewriting, when the query values
(i.e., x=foo, y=bar) are available to server.R, the application would be
able to auto-select form inputs (for ui.R) which corresponding to the
parameters in the URI.

I'm hoping to use the shiny server in this fashion, and not as a single
entry point application at http://example.org/ . If this is not the job
of Shiny server, I would appreciate a pointer, if any.

Thanks,

-Sarven

messages.subject: Re: URI Rewrites
parts: Oh, OK. Sorry, URL rewriting is not directly possible using Shiny Server. I think your best bet would be to proxy Shiny Server behind nginx or apache and use their URL rewriting capabilities. Proxying behind nginx or apache is a good idea in any case.

messages.author: 563435cd1cb6a261
messages.subject: Re: URI Rewrites
parts:
I'm not sure if I completely follow.

Okay, then lets say that Nginx or Apache handles the proxying, and
passes an URL like the following for Shiny server:

http://localhost/?x=foo&y=bar

How can I access those query parameters from shiny.R?


After digging around a bit, as I understand it, I need to do something
like (perhaps in main.js?);

var url = require('url');
var urlParams = url.parse(request.url, true);
var query = urlParams.query;

and have query available from server.R, so that:

print(query.x) #Returns foo

print(query.y) #Returns bar

If that makes sense, how can I access global variables from nodejs from
server.R?

I've also looked into express and express-rewrite:

var rewriter = require('express-rewrite');
var app = express.createServer();
app.configure(function() {
app.use(rewriter);
app.use(server.router);
});
server.get('/:x/:y', rewriter.rewrite('/?x=$1&y=$2'));

which I didn't get far with but I think the issue still boils down to
being able to access certain variables from shiny.R.

Pardon my ignorance as I'm trying to figure out all this. I'm completely
new to Shiny server and node.js :)

Thanks,

-Sarven

Oh, you can access the query string directly from your server.R file using the new clientData feature:
http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#client-data

I'm not sure if this is in the CRAN version of Shiny or if you need to install it from GitHub:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("shiny", "rstudio")
